entries.definition: the kind of work someone does
entries.example: The form asks for your occupation, not the name of your employer.

entries.definition: a type of work usually requiring specialized education or training
entries.example: She entered the teaching profession after completing her training.

entries.definition: specialized knowledge or skill gained through experience
entries.example: The project combines technical expertise with local knowledge.

entries.definition: the process of finding and selecting people for work
entries.example: The recruitment process includes a practical task and an interview.

entries.definition: a person being considered for a position
entries.example: Each candidate receives the same information before the assessment.

entries.definition: someone who formally requests a job or opportunity
entries.example: The applicant explained how her experience matched the role.

entries.definition: an available job that has not been filled
entries.example: The vacancy was advertised on the community notice board.

entries.definition: a period of supervised work experience
entries.example: The internship gave him experience of working with real clients.

entries.definition: training in a trade through supervised practical work
entries.example: Her apprenticeship combines workshop practice with formal instruction.

entries.definition: an initial period during which job suitability is assessed
entries.example: During probation, the supervisor meets new staff regularly.

entries.definition: a structured discussion evaluating someone’s work
entries.example: The appraisal considers achievements as well as support needs.

entries.definition: how effectively someone carries out work or an activity
entries.example: The review looks at performance across several tasks.

entries.definition: the amount of useful output produced from time or resources
entries.example: The team measured productivity without ignoring errors or staff workload.

entries.definition: the ability to achieve results with little waste
entries.example: Better file organization improved efficiency without increasing working hours.

entries.definition: the amount of work someone is expected to do
entries.example: Her workload became more manageable after two tasks were reassigned.

entries.definition: work done beyond normal working hours
entries.example: The manager asked whether overtime was necessary or simply routine.

entries.definition: something that encourages a person to act
entries.example: The travel allowance provided an incentive to attend the training.

entries.definition: pay and related benefits received for work
entries.example: The offer explains compensation as well as working conditions.

entries.definition: money provided regularly for a particular expense
entries.example: The transport allowance helps staff reach the remote office.

entries.definition: repayment of money someone has spent on an approved expense
entries.example: Keep your receipts if you need reimbursement for travel.

entries.definition: a benefit or right provided under an agreement or rule
entries.example: The contract explains each worker’s entitlement to leave.

entries.definition: a formal complaint about unfair treatment at work
entries.example: The organization has a procedure for raising a grievance.

entries.definition: the loss or suspension of a job because the work is no longer needed
entries.example: The company announced a layoff after the project ended.

entries.definition: the formal act of leaving a job voluntarily
entries.example: Her resignation letter included the proposed final working day.

entries.definition: the ending of someone’s employment by an employer
entries.example: The handbook explains the procedure that can lead to dismissal.

entries.definition: giving another person responsibility for a task
entries.example: Effective delegation includes clear limits and the resources to act.

entries.definition: to oversee work and provide direction or support
entries.example: An experienced technician will supervise the repair.

entries.definition: to arrange connected activities so they work together
entries.example: We need to coordinate deliveries with the workshop schedule.

entries.definition: to decide which tasks matter most or should happen first
entries.example: The team will prioritize safety problems before minor visual changes.

entries.definition: to assign time, money, or other resources to a purpose
entries.example: We allocate part of the budget to maintenance.

entries.definition: to put a plan or decision into practice
entries.example: Staff will implement the new process after training.

entries.definition: to carry out a planned action or task
entries.example: The team must execute each stage in the agreed order.

entries.definition: to simplify a process by removing unnecessary steps
entries.example: The office will streamline registration without removing essential checks.

entries.definition: an overall plan for achieving a longer-term aim
entries.example: The strategy includes both immediate repairs and future training.

entries.definition: a specific result someone aims to reach
entries.example: The sales target was revised when the opening date changed.

entries.definition: an important stage showing progress in a project
entries.example: Finishing the working model was the first milestone.

entries.definition: a defined result or item that a project must produce
entries.example: The final deliverable is a tested guide with clear instructions.

entries.definition: someone affected by or interested in a decision or project
entries.example: Each stakeholder had a chance to explain what the change would mean.

entries.definition: someone who starts and develops a business
entries.example: The entrepreneur tested demand before renting a larger shop.

entries.definition: a business or organized commercial activity
entries.example: The small enterprise repairs devices that would otherwise be discarded.

entries.definition: money received from sales or other business activity before costs
entries.example: Higher revenue did not automatically mean higher profit.

entries.definition: the rate at which employees leave and are replaced
entries.example: High staff turnover prompted a review of working conditions.

entries.definition: money spent on an activity or over a period
entries.example: The report separates routine expenditure from one-time purchases.

entries.definition: money or effort committed for a possible future benefit
entries.example: Training is an investment that may support future improvements.

entries.definition: something owned that has economic value
entries.example: The organization records each major asset in its accounts.

entries.definition: a financial obligation or amount owed
entries.example: The unpaid loan remains a liability until it is repaid.

entries.definition: the organized process of obtaining goods or services
entries.example: The procurement rules require clear reasons for choosing a supplier.

entries.definition: a record or supply of goods and materials held
entries.example: The inventory showed that several spare parts were missing.

entries.definition: the organization of moving and supplying people or goods
entries.example: The event’s logistics included transport, storage, and arrival times.

entries.definition: to arrange for an outside provider to do work
entries.example: The workshop may outsource printing while keeping design work in-house.
